newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes down slightly vs US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes down slightly vs US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan ended down slightly at 8.2975 against the U.S. dollar on Wednesday from Tuesday's 8.2971 on the Shanghai-based interbank foreign exchange market.
Dealers said the yuan moved stably after yesterday's sharp rises supported by the news that China's trade surplus in September increased to $3.2 billion from $3 billion in August.
The yuan opened slightly down at 8.2973 and fell further to an intra-day low of 8.2982 early in the session. It then rose to move around 8.2975 for most of the trading, hitting a high of 8.2972.
Trading was dull with most done at 8.2975, traders said.
"The trade surplus data released yesterday still supported the yuan's strong uptrend," one dealer said.
"More dollar supplies will push the yuan higher," he added.

"The central bank announced that the interest rate subsidy (on deposits of three or more years) for November is 4.04 percent, but the news had little impact in the yuan's movement today," a second dealer said.
"But the rate shows that inflation has rebounded to some extent, which will affect the yuan's supply indirectly," he added.
Dealers expect the yuan to move in a range of 8.2970 and 8.2980 tomorrow.
The yuan closed up at 7.3903 from 7.4222 against 100 Japanese yen and rose to 1.0729 from 1.0733 against the Hong Kong dollar.
